attrs.def: A disposition to undergo pathological processes that exists in an organism because of one or more disorders in that organism.
A disease that manifests in a defined anatomical structure.
A disease resulting from the presence and activity of a microbial, viral, fungal or parasitic agent.
A disease characterized by abnormally rapid cell division.
A disease that involves errors in metabolic processes of building or degradation of molecules.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in the heart or blood vessels.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in the airways, lungs or pleura.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in the central or peripheral nervous system.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in the digestive tract or its accessory organs.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in an endocrine gland.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in the kidneys or urinary tract.
A disease of anatomical entity that results from a dysfunction of the immune system.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in bones, joints or skeletal muscle.
A disease of anatomical entity that is located in the skin or its appendages.
A disease of anatomical entity that affects the blood or blood-forming tissues.
A cardiovascular system disease that is located in the heart.
A heart disease in which atherosclerotic plaque narrows the coronary arteries and reduces blood flow to the myocardium.
A coronary artery disease characterized by episodic chest pain caused by transient myocardial ischemia.
A heart disease in which the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the needs of the body.
A heart disease characterized by rapid and irregular contraction of the atria.
A cardiovascular system disease characterized by persistently elevated arterial blood pressure.
A cardiovascular system disease characterized by the build-up of lipid-laden plaque in the intima of arteries.
A cardiovascular system disease that affects the blood vessels supplying the brain.
A cerebrovascular disease in which an arterial occlusion causes focal infarction of brain tissue.
A cerebrovascular disease caused by rupture of a blood vessel and bleeding into or around the brain.
A respiratory system disease that is located in the lung.
A lung disease that is located in the bronchi.
A bronchial disease characterized by productive cough lasting at least three months in two consecutive years.
A chronic obstructive pulmonary disease characterized by permanent enlargement and destruction of the alveolar walls.
A lung disease characterized by inflammation of the alveoli, usually caused by infection.
A pneumonia that is caused by a bacterial infection.
A pneumonia that is caused by a viral infection.
A cancer that originates in the tissues of the lung.
A lung cancer that is not a small cell carcinoma; includes adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and large cell carcinoma.
A lung cancer composed of small cells with neuroendocrine features.
A disease of cellular proliferation that is malignant and primary, characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation, local cell invasion and metastasis.
A cancer that is located in the colon or rectum.
An infectious disease that is caused by a bacterium.
An infectious disease that is caused by a virus.
A viral infectious disease of the respiratory tract caused by influenza A or B virus.
A hepatitis that is caused by a hepatotropic virus.
A viral hepatitis caused by hepatitis B virus.
A viral hepatitis caused by hepatitis C virus.
A nervous system disease characterized by progressive loss of structure or function of neurons.
A neurodegenerative disease characterized by loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra.
A nervous system disease characterized by immune-mediated demyelination in the central nervous system.
A nervous system disease characterized by an enduring predisposition to generate epileptic seizures.
A disease of metabolism characterized by chronic hyperglycemia resulting from defects in insulin secretion, insulin action, or both.
An endocrine system disease that is located in the thyroid gland.
A thyroid disease characterized by insufficient production of thyroid hormones.
A thyroid disease characterized by excessive production of thyroid hormones.
A thyroid disease in which the immune system targets thyroid antigens.
An autoimmune thyroid disease in which thyroid-stimulating antibodies cause hyperthyroidism and diffuse goiter.
An endocrine system disease that is located in the pituitary gland.
An immune system disease in which the immune response is directed against the body’s own tissues.
A liver disease characterized by inflammation of the liver parenchyma.
A gastrointestinal system disease that is located in the liver.
An alcoholic liver disease characterized by acute inflammation and necrosis of the liver.
A liver disease characterized by diffuse fibrosis and regenerative nodules replacing normal liver architecture.
A gastrointestinal system disease that is located in the intestine.
An intestinal disease characterized by chronic inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract.
An inflammatory bowel disease characterized by continuous mucosal inflammation of the colon and rectum.
A gastrointestinal system disease characterized by inflammation of the gastric mucosa.
An intestinal disease in which gluten triggers immune-mediated damage of the small intestinal mucosa.
A urinary system disease that is located in the kidney.
A kidney disease characterized by inflammation of the renal glomeruli.
A musculoskeletal system disease characterized by chronic immune-mediated inflammation of synovial joints.
A musculoskeletal system disease characterized by degeneration of articular cartilage and remodelling of subchondral bone.
A musculoskeletal system disease characterized by low bone mass and deterioration of bone microarchitecture.
An integumentary system disease characterized by immune-mediated hyperproliferation of keratinocytes forming scaly plaques.
A hematologic disease characterized by a decrease in the total amount of hemoglobin or red blood cells.
An anemia caused by insufficient iron for hemoglobin synthesis.
A material entity that is part of a human organism.
An anatomical entity that consists of multiple organs that together perform a common function.
An anatomical entity that is a discrete structural unit performing a specific function.
An anatomical entity that is part of an organ.
An anatomical entity consisting of similar cells and intercellular matrix.
An anatomical system that circulates blood through the body.
An anatomical system that carries out gas exchange.
An anatomical system that coordinates actions by transmitting signals between body parts.
An anatomical system that ingests and digests food and absorbs nutrients.
An anatomical system of glands that secrete hormones into the blood.
An anatomical system that produces, stores and eliminates urine.
An anatomical system that protects the organism against disease.
An anatomical system that provides form, support, stability and movement.
An anatomical system that forms the external covering of the body.
An organ that pumps blood through the circulatory system.
A tissue that forms the muscular wall of the heart.
An organ that conveys blood through the body.
A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart.
An artery that supplies blood to the myocardium.
An organ of the respiratory system in which gas exchange takes place.
An organ part that conducts air from the trachea into the lungs.
An organ part of the lung where gas exchange with the blood occurs.
An organ of the central nervous system enclosed in the cranium.
An organ part that forms the outer layer of grey matter of the cerebrum.
An organ part of the medial temporal lobe involved in memory consolidation.
An organ part of the midbrain containing dopaminergic neurons.
An organ part of the forebrain that links the nervous system to the endocrine system.
An organ of the central nervous system extending from the brainstem through the vertebral canal.
An organ at the base of the brain that secretes hormones regulating other endocrine glands.
An organ in the neck that produces thyroid hormones.
An organ with exocrine digestive and endocrine functions.
An organ part of the pancreas that contains hormone-producing cells, including insulin-secreting beta cells.
An organ of the digestive system that metabolizes nutrients and detoxifies the blood.
An organ of the digestive tract between the esophagus and the duodenum.
An organ of the digestive tract extending from the pylorus to the anus.
An organ part of the intestine where most nutrient absorption occurs.
An organ part of the large intestine between the cecum and the rectum.
An organ of the renal system that filters blood and produces urine.
An organ part of the kidney consisting of a capillary tuft where blood is filtered.
An organ that covers the external surface of the body.
An organ composed mainly of mineralized bone tissue.
An organ part that forms a movable articulation between bones.
A tissue consisting of plasma and blood cells that circulates through the cardiovascular system.
A clinically observable abnormality reported by a patient or detected on examination.
A sign or symptom consisting of an unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage.
A pain that is perceived in the chest.
A pain that is perceived in the head.
A pain that is perceived in the abdomen.
A pain that is perceived in a joint.
A pain that is perceived in a muscle.
A sign or symptom that involves the respiratory system.
A respiratory symptom consisting of a sudden, forceful expulsion of air from the lungs.
A respiratory symptom consisting of a high-pitched whistling sound during breathing.
A respiratory symptom consisting of coughing up blood.
A sign or symptom that affects general well-being or the body as a whole.
A constitutional symptom consisting of an elevated body temperature.
A constitutional symptom consisting of a subjective feeling of tiredness that is not relieved by rest.
A constitutional symptom consisting of an unintended reduction in body weight.
A constitutional symptom consisting of an unintended increase in body weight.
A constitutional symptom consisting of excessive sweating during sleep.
A sign or symptom that involves the nervous system.
A neurological symptom consisting of an involuntary, rhythmic oscillation of a body part.
A neurological symptom consisting of a transient occurrence of signs due to abnormal synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.
A neurological symptom consisting of a reduced ability to store or recall information.
A neurological symptom consisting of slowness of initiation and execution of movement.
A neurological symptom consisting of abnormal skin sensations such as tingling or numbness.
A neurological symptom consisting of weakness of one side of the body.
A sign or symptom that involves the digestive system.
A gastrointestinal symptom consisting of an urge to vomit.
A gastrointestinal symptom consisting of abnormally frequent, loose bowel movements.
A gastrointestinal symptom consisting of the passage of fresh blood per anus.
A sign consisting of yellow discoloration of the skin and sclerae due to hyperbilirubinemia.
A sign consisting of an abnormally large production of urine.
A symptom consisting of excessive thirst and fluid intake.
A sign consisting of the presence of blood in the urine.
A sign consisting of abnormal accumulation of fluid in the interstitium.
A symptom consisting of an unpleasant awareness of the heartbeat.
A symptom consisting of an itching sensation that provokes the desire to scratch.
A sign consisting of enlargement of the thyroid gland.
A sign consisting of accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity.
A symptom consisting of the loss of the sense of smell.
A sign consisting of a deviation of the blood glucose concentration from the normal range.
An abnormal blood glucose concentration below the normal range.
A sign consisting of the need to wake at night to pass urine.

A coronary artery disease characterized by necrosis of myocardial tissue caused by prolonged ischemia.
